scope: Offline interpretation of one frozen release relay run, steady delay or burst; no new acceptance threshold or causal performance attribution.

cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

headedLaunch.scope: Window-mode environment control, not a production code change; proxy, input, audio/context, CPU setup, and native GPU arguments are unchanged.

interpretation: Response formal cohort uses each page performance clock, offsetting responsiveness.startedAt against measure.started. Metrics condition on non-null observations and changed masks; all missing/status counts remain visible.

Before-formal is observed active warmup and after-formal is the observed tail. Intents are grouped by schedule time; observationPhases separately retains where submission, first wire and presentation completed, including crossings of the formal boundary.

The original formal/first-last-frame-filtered cohort is retained. continuousWindow adds a separate half-open first-180 to first-limit clock interval; its end observation remains an elapsed/state-gap boundary witness but is excluded from its callback distributions. A later rollback below limit cannot move tail observations back into this continuous formal window.
firstWire is the JavaScript send observer after native capture/serialization, before transport send. It establishes neither remote ACK nor remote capture.
Presentation is a newer simulation frontier with increased renderer submissions, observed after play.frame. It establishes neither pixel movement nor physical scanout.
A superseded uncaptured intent is a missed synthetic edge. pendingAgeAtEnd is its historical age, not a continuously held input or a freeze.
Relay selects kind-1 packets in both directions at scheduling. packetSummary includes steady delay and any burst; sendApi is the relay WebSocket API boundary, not peer delivery or native acceptance.
Relay senderFrameBands and burst frame windows use sender frame annotations, not exact browser/relay wall-clock synchronization. No remote receipt or native input acceptance latency is inferred.

Pacing distributions are sampled callback observations, not wall-time fractions. missingRemoteInputs comes from the live export, not from configured delay. historicalReplayRemainingTicks is max(0, predictionFrontier-currentFrame), not rollback depth.

Rollback totals sum adjacent post-callback cumulative counter differences. The first sample has no predecessor. An interval beginning inside a window can have its prior sample outside; the frozen smoothness summary separately retains its original first/last subtraction. No per-correction depth can be recovered from these aggregates.

observedTimeWindows includes every sample between the first and last formal observations, including historical replay below frame 180. The frozen smoothness summary uses its original per-sample frame criterion.

The original frame-filtered summary can splice nonconsecutive callbacks if frame reaches limit and later rewinds below it. Its RAF/presentation gap values are preserved as historical outputs, not accepted as actual scheduling gaps; legacyFrameFilter lists the skipped and re-entered rows.

New-state intervals use the frozen harness rAF timestamp convention; observation gaps and C++ work are separately retained. Full-session and boundary-crossing intervals prevent a formal frame filter from hiding warmup/tail gaps. over50ms retains observations for inspection and is not a new gate. No physical-presentation or CPU-time claim follows.

formalWindow.cohortRule: scheduledAtMs within first/last formal sample observations, inclusive; never select by successful capture/presentation

continuousWindow.rule: Half-open response-clock interval from the first sample reaching frame >=180 to the first sample reaching frame >=limit; that terminal observation and all later samples stay in after-formal, even if rollback later lowers frame.

legacyFrameFilter.rule: Original formal/summary frame criterion is preserved. It may leave and re-enter after the first limit observation; skipped callback rows must not become a physical RAF stall.

rollback.reason: The frozen release samples contain cumulative correction/resimulation counters, but no restore target or per-correction replay span. Counter deltas, prediction lead and remaining replay are not rollback depth.

injection.packetScope: E9NP version 4 kind 1; ACK-only and redundant input included; non-input control/hash/signaling untouched; relay has no separate RTC repair lane.
injection.jitterAlgorithm: Per-sender LCG 1664525*x+1013904223, seed 0x915ab+sender; same formula as legacy client impairment. Relay forwarding order can differ.
injection.burstClock: First non-empty E9NP input receive in this relay process; distinct from browser active time.

host.scope: Read-only host CPU counters and candidate process CPU counters. No performance samples are excluded or reweighted.
limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
Overflow and sampling failures make this evidence incomplete; they are never a reason to silently remove a game result.
